text:
acme-integrator: Hey team, our integration started returning 403 only for the /v1/generate endpoint this morning. Embeddings still succeed. No code changes on our side. We're seeing this for a handful of customers behind our SSO stack.

maya-cs: Sorry about the hit — can you share a redacted request + failure response (headers ok to strip api key)? Also, does retrying ever succeed?

acme-integrator: Here's a minimal repro we captured. Embeddings request (works):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGci... (REDACTED)" \n  -H "X-SSO-Scopes: eyJzY29wZXMiOlsiZW1iZWRkaW5nIiwicmVyYW5rIl19" \n  -d '{"input":"hi"}'
```
Response 200.

Generate request (403):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGci... (SAME TOKEN)" \n  -H "X-SSO-Scopes: eyJzY29wZXMiOlsiZW1iZWRkaW5nIiwicmVyYW5rIl19" \
  -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'
```
Response 403 JSON: `{"error":"insufficient_scope","message":"missing: inference.generate"}`

acme-integrator: We noticed the X-SSO-Scopes header arriving at your edge sometimes looks like `eyJzY29wZXMiOlsiZW1iZWRkaW5nIiwicmVyYW5rIl19` and other times like `eyJzY29wZXMiOlsiZW1iZWRkaW5nIiwicmVyYW5rIl19` (same). We're confused because embeddings works but generate doesn't.

jordan-eng: Thanks for the repro — quick sanity check: are you sure the token is identical? Token-based routing can hit different auth code paths. Can you paste the full header list from your proxy logs (redact token body)?

acme-integrator: Pasted from our sidecar logs: `X-SSO-Scopes: eyJzY29wZXMiOlsiZW1iZWRkaW5nIiwicmVyYW5rIl19` (base64, ends with 'Il19'). Upstream (our ingress) shows `X-SSO-Scopes: eyJzY29wZXMiOlsiZW1iZWRkaW5nIiwicmVyYW5rIl1` (missing trailing 2 chars). We discovered our proxy strips trailing '=' padding in custom headers for some hops.

maya-cs: Interesting — our auth pipeline expects the scope claim encoded as base64 JSON and decodes it server-side. If padding or chars are stripped base64 fails and we fall back to token-only scan which only preserved embeddings permission for your tenant. Could explain why embeddings works and generate doesn't.

li-devops: Can you confirm the exact decoded JSON when present? Also, which proxy/version strips padding? We need to replicate.

acme-integrator: When intact, base64 decodes to `{"scopes":["embedding","rerank","inference.generate"]}`. When stripped (missing padding), decode fails.

jordan-eng: That matches reproduction. We reproduced locally by sending header with the last '=' removed and our auth decoder returned null scopes -> defaulted to minimal entitlements (embeddings only). Code pointer: auth/service/parse_sso_header.go -> b64 decode returns error and we swallow it. Filed quick fix to log decode errors (ENG-4532).

sam-plat: For a short-term mitigation, we can accept a second header `X-SSO-Scopes-Alt` with a URL-safe base64 encoding or fallback to parsing a JWT claim if present. But best fix is making the auth decoder tolerant to missing padding and to log when decode fails.

acme-integrator: We can patch our proxy to stop trimming padding. Which rollout looks fastest on your side? Customers are seeing intermittent 403s across regions.

maya-cs: We'll push the auth logging hotfix immediately to catch incoming decode errors and add a fallback path. ETA ~2 hours. For customers blocked today, add them to a allowlist requiring explicit full-key entitlements (we can grant temporary org-scoped admin key). I'll DM the list.

li-devops: Also noted: some edge caches rewrite headers for size reasons. We're auditing that config. Please share proxy vendor/version and any hop details.

acme-integrator: Proxy vendor: CloudProxy v3.8.1, we enabled `trim-http-headers` for bandwidth. We'll disable for the SSO header and push a config change now.

deploy-bot: deploy queued by maya-cs -> auth-service -> canary to us-east-1

jordan-eng: Root cause summary for the ticket: SSO scope header was base64 JSON; intermediary proxy trimmed header padding resulting in base64 decode failures in auth pipeline causing scopes to be treated as absent -> default minimal entitlements (embeddings) -> 403 on inference.generate. Fixes: 1) make auth decode tolerant and log (hotfix), 2) recommend proxy config change to preserve header padding (customer action), 3) long-term: support URL-safe base64 or JWT-based scope claim.

maya-cs: Marking this resolved for now after fixes roll out; will reopen if we see further 403s for the customer. acme-integrator, please confirm once your proxy change is live. :thumbsup:

acme-integrator: Will do — config change applied, I'm seeing immediate green for generate in our staging. Thanks all!
